critiques.target: E017 lesson ('3-seed noise is ~0.3–0.4 pp, diffs under 0.6 pp uninterpretable')
critiques.issue: This lesson rests on two outliers. Seven recipes have both a seeds 0–2 mean and a held-out mean. The seeds 0–2 minus held-out offsets are E010 +0.08, E016 +0.43, E017 −0.40, E018 −0.07, E020 −0.05, E021 +0.03 and E022 −0.08. Five of the seven sit within ±0.08 pp, which is what iid seeds predict (SD ≈ 0.16 pp). Only E016 and E017, the two crop implementations, are far off, and in opposite directions. So either a mask-vs-gather crop × seed interaction exists, or the E016 held-out run differed in some way (build, cache, harness path). E016's seeds 0–2 result was never rebuilt or re-run.
critiques.suggestion: Re-run E016 through ar.py from a fresh build to check whether 0.7607 reproduces. Then pool the 7 offsets as the empirical noise estimate (RMS ≈ 0.23 pp) instead of the worst case. Pre-register keep decisions on the held-out 10-seed mean. A 10-seed difference SE is about 0.09–0.1 pp, and the E016 vs E017 'identical distribution' gap of 0.13 pp fits that.

critiques.issue: The 'wd ×0.5 helps' claim rests on E016 seeds 0–2 (+0.33 vs E015). That is exactly the seed set later shown to be +0.43 pp lucky. On held-out seeds the gain over E010 is +0.24 pp (0.7540 → 0.7564), and that comparison also includes E015's compile-mode change, which never got a held-out run. The −0.24 pp held-out drop at ×0.25 (E022) has the same size and is called a refutation. Both effects are about 2–2.5σ, and confidence 0.70 overstates them.
critiques.suggestion: Lower confidence to about 0.5. If accuracy is needed to fund trims, run wd ×1 vs ×0.5 on the current tip (E017) with held-out seeds 3–12, so the comparison is a single-factor paired test on one build lineage.

critiques.target: H1.3.1, H1.3.4, E014 (LS, LR floor, Muon lr 'flat')
critiques.issue: Each was discarded on a 3-seed difference of ≤0.1 pp, with no held-out run. The tree records them as refuted at confidence 0.08–0.10, which is far more certainty than ±0.2–0.4 pp noise allows. All three also ran on the pre-E016 base (wd ×1). LS, wd and lr×wd interact as regularizers, so the optima may have moved after wd was halved.
critiques.suggestion: Re-label them as 'no effect larger than ~0.4 pp' (inconclusive) instead of refuted. If you revisit, test on the current tip with held-out seeds: LS 0.2 or 0.1, and Muon lr ×2 (0.48), which E014's upward trend points to.

critiques.issue: E006 switched the optimizer to Muon and the batch size from 1024 to 2000 at the same time. H1.2.1's stated test ('SGD tuned at batch 2000') was never run, yet E006 is logged as supporting it. The +0.66 pp could come from batch size or step count, not Muon. The result is also surprising: higher accuracy with about half the optimizer steps (~238). That suggests a step-count/noise-scale effect that no hypothesis covers.
critiques.suggestion: Mark E006 as inconclusive for H1.2.1. Run H1.2.2 (Nesterov SGD at batch 2000 on the tip). Add a batch-size dial under Muon (1500 / 2500) to H1 or H4.2, since fewer, larger steps may be a cheaper lever than cutting epochs.

Held-out slope ~0.44 pp/epoch from 0.7577 predicts ~0.7555 held-out at 9.0 true epochs and ~6.2 s.

critiques.target: H4.2.3 and the epoch lineage of E008–E010
critiques.issue: H4.2.3 is still open at 0.70, but E012's per-epoch timing already settles it. The 10 loops (four at 24 px, then 28 px, then two full 32 px loops and a half loop) fit 9.5 true epochs with a 40/30/30 split almost exactly. The lineage is also inconsistent. E009 and E010 say 'E007 recipe at 9 epochs', but their times (6.99 s, and E010 is −4.8% vs E008) match the E008 base. E008's '9→8.5' label means 10→9.5 true. Every per-epoch slope in the tree is built on mislabelled epochs.
critiques.suggestion: Close H4.2.3 as supported. Restate all recipes in optimizer steps, and fix the E009/E010 parent attribution so slope estimates use the correct baselines.

critiques.issue: H2.3 calls resizing a 'near-linear time dial that costs little'. But both of its tagged experiments refute (E011-, E018-), and the exchange rates get worse fast: E007 ~3.6 s/pp (3-seed, vs E006), E011 ~1.0 s/pp, E018 ~0.8 s/pp (held-out). E018 is surprising. Changing only the 28 px phase to 24 px cost 0.68 pp held-out, more than the whole 24/28/32 schedule cost against all-32 in E007 (0.59 pp, 3-seed). Possible explanations: (a) the 28 px phase overlaps the peak-LR window where most features are learned; (b) the single 24→32 jump causes a larger object-size/BN-statistics shift than two smaller jumps; (c) E007's 0.59 pp cost was underestimated because E006 was a lucky 3-seed draw.
critiques.suggestion: Mark H2.3 as 'supported only for the mild E007 schedule'. To separate (a) from (b), run a 24/28/32 schedule with the 28 px phase moved later, or a 28/32-only schedule. Also run H2.3.3 (BN recalibration at 32 px) on E018. Consider the reverse direction too: less resizing (e.g. 30/30/40) combined with an epoch cut.

critiques.issue: Several hypotheses stay 'open' although a pre-registered refuting result exists. H2.2.3 (E017-, −0.5%), H2.5.1 (E021-, 1.0 s/pp, worse than epochs), H1.5.3 (E022-) and H4.1.3 (E016 held-out 0.7564, which is below the 0.757 floor and 0.43 pp off, outside the 0.05–0.3 window) all fall in this group. H1.2.1, H1.5.2 and H4.2.2 are open with + evidence from single 3-seed diffs within noise. E010's −0.25 pp has no held-out baseline for E008.
critiques.suggestion: Set H2.2.3, H2.5.1, H1.5.3 and H4.1.3 to refuted. For H1.5.2, either run a held-out 576-vs-512 comparison on the tip or record that E010's width cost is unknown. The current 1.4 s/pp rate could easily be anywhere in 0.7–3 s/pp.

critiques.issue: This claim was never measured. H2.2.4 (achieved TFLOP/s) is open, and E011's '95% pixel-proportional' only shows the step is GPU-bound, not that the GPU kernels are efficient. E021 found time fell only 7.8% for a 15.5% MAC cut, a sign of poor tensor-core use at small spatial sizes. A GPU-bound step can still run at 60 TFLOP/s instead of 110.
critiques.suggestion: Run H2.2.4 now; it is one profiler trace. If achieved throughput is below ~90 TFLOP/s, a systems lever remains that no current hypothesis covers. Options include padded channel counts, bigger batches at low resolution, and cuDNN algorithm selection for the 7×7/3×3 maps.

critiques.issue: Several low-cost accuracy boosters were proposed but never run. These include BN recalibration after the EMA swap (H1.3.6, H2.3.3), even though the E005 lesson called end-of-training noise reduction first-order, as well as plain EMA vs lookahead (H1.3.5), the Muon NS-iteration cut (H1.2.3), dropping a group-1 conv (H2.5.2) and hard-example selection (H2.4). Also absent: warm-up length or LR-schedule shape, crop padding / translate magnitude, a clean (unaugmented) final epoch, and wider group 3 with fewer epochs.
critiques.suggestion: Prioritize the moves that are time-neutral or cut time: BN recal (<0.15 s), NS 5→3, and the −0.5 epoch trim. Use held-out seeds for every accuracy decision.

critiques.issue: Feasibility is decided on fixed seeds 0–2. Because RNG-consumption changes re-roll the seeds 0–2 offset by up to ±0.4 pp, any 'harmless' code change can pass or fail the bar by luck. E020 (held-out 0.7533, 5.86 s) would very likely pass the official 40-seed 0.75 bar but misses the local 0.753 bar by 0.02 pp. The loop can therefore drift into rerolling RNG paths until seeds 0–2 come out lucky.
critiques.suggestion: Add an explicit rule: a keep needs both a seeds 0–2 mean ≥ 0.753 and a held-out 10-seed mean of at least ~0.755. Never keep a change whose only effect is a different RNG stream (as E017's gather crop was) when the motivation is accuracy.

critiques.target: Rule compliance: eval under cudagraphs + error_on_recompile
critiques.issue: Since E008, error_on_recompile=True is set after build, and E015 switched to max-autotune with cudagraphs. The rules require finite logits for any B from 1 to 1024 within 5 s. If eval goes through the compiled or cudagraph model, any batch size not warmed up in build (e.g. 333) would raise or recompile, with recapture plus autotune possibly exceeding 5 s. The tree only records checks at B in {1, 7, 512, 1024} (E003).
critiques.suggestion: Check offline that eval runs on an eager or dynamic-shape path that is exempt from error_on_recompile. Then sweep B over all of 1..1024 (or a dense random sample) on the tip, checking time and finiteness, before relying on any result after E015.

structured_output.summary: The tip (E017: 6.55 s, seeds 0–2 0.7537, held-out 0.7577) is solid. The tree's accounting of evidence is weaker than its results. (1) The noise model is inconsistent. H4.1 and H4.1.1 are marked supported, although E019 broke bit-reproducibility for cudagraph builds. Meanwhile the '≥0.6 pp unresolvable' lesson generalizes from two outliers, E016 and E017, while five of the seven seeds 0–2 vs held-out offsets are ≤0.08 pp. E016's 0.7607 was never rebuilt. (2) Several conclusions rest on 3-seed differences within noise but are recorded as refuted or supported with high confidence: LS 0.2 vs 0.3, the LR floor, Muon lr, the 512 width, and the size of the wd ×0.5 gain (about +0.24 pp held-out, confounded with E015). (3) There are bookkeeping errors. H2.2.3, H2.5.1, H1.5.3 and H4.1.3 have refuting results but remain open. H1.2.1 and H4.2.4 claim support from experiments that did not test their stated predictions: E006 changed batch size and optimizer together, and E020 ran only the −1.0 epoch point. H4.2.3 is effectively settled by E012's timing (9.5 true epochs), and the E009/E010 parent labels contradict their times. (4) There are surprises the Lvl1s do not explain. Muon at batch 2000 gained accuracy with half the steps, suggesting step-count or noise-scale is the lever, not Muon. Dropping only the 28 px phase (E018) cost more than the whole resizing schedule did in E007, which points to a phase-timing or resolution-jump mechanism. H2.2's '≤5% systems headroom' was never measured, and E021's sublinear width scaling hints at poor tensor-core use. (5) Untested cheap levers: the −0.5 true-epoch trim (best next step), BN recalibration after the EMA swap, NS 5→3, batch-size dial under Muon, and less aggressive resizing traded for epochs. (6) There is a compliance risk to verify: error_on_recompile combined with cudagraphs may break eval at batch sizes not warmed up in build, while the rules require any B from 1 to 1024 within 5 s.
